processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melted in an induction furnace under Ar atmosphere.
Cast to round bars, 25 mm in diameter.
Cast ingots reheated to 1200 °C for 30 min prior to hot rolling.
Solution-treated for 2 h at 1100 °C under Ar, then quenched in water; parent process of the long annealing.
Long annealing treatment for the 8Al steel is 600 °C/24 h, producing cuboidal nanosized κ-carbides; corresponds to the '8Al, 1 h/600 °C/24 h' state.

structures.overall_structure: Long annealed 8Al steel contains a uniform distribution of intragranular cuboidal nanosized κ-carbides in an austenite matrix; the high volume fraction of precipitates produces narrow matrix channels of about 2–3 nm width.

phases_present.texture: cube/cube orientation relationship with the austenite matrix

precipitates.distribution: uniform, intragranular; narrow matrix channels of about 2–3 nm width between precipitates
precipitates.coherency: cube/cube orientation relationship with the austenite matrix; shearable by dislocations

structures.overall_structure: Upon straining to 0.15 true strain the long annealed 8Al steel develops planar dislocation substructures consisting of dense dislocation arrays spaced between 100 and 300 nm; cuboidal κ-carbides within the arrays are frequently sheared by dislocations.

phases_present.texture: cube/cube orientation relationship with the austenite matrix

defects.type: planar dislocation substructures consisting of dense dislocation arrays spaced between 100 and 300 nm

precipitates.distribution: within dense dislocation arrays; frequently sheared by dislocations
precipitates.coherency: cube/cube orientation relationship with the austenite matrix; shearable

phase_interfaces.coherence: cube/cube orientation relationship with the austenite matrix

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Within the dense dislocation arrays, cuboidal κ-carbides are frequently sheared by dislocations; shearing of the cuboidal κ-carbides enhances planar slip and results in the combination of high strength (YS 990 MPa, UTS 1180 MPa) and ductility (UE 37%).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: planar slip promoted by shearable precipitates
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The enhancement of planar slip by shearing of cuboidal κ-carbides results in planar dislocation substructures; plasticity is mainly concentrated through the dislocation boundaries of such substructures.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar slip; planar dislocation substructures (dense dislocation arrays) stabilized by shearable nanosized κ-carbides.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical tensile samples with gauges of 6 mm diameter and 40 mm length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Interrupted tensile tests to different strain levels were also performed.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Nearly linear stress–strain curve after yielding, without a concave (multiple-hardening) shape (see Figure 1).

strain_hardening_rate.value: 8Al steels ~2 GPa at the early stages of deformation (lower hardening capacity than 2Al steels ~2.6 GPa); single hardening regime fairly constant during deformation
8Al-600°C/24h single nearly constant hardening regime close to 2 GPa; drops to ~1.9 GPa around 1200 MPa, broad maximum near 2.2 GPa at ~1350 MPa, then falls to ~1.2 GPa at ~1550 MPa

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Long annealing (600 °C/24 h) vs short annealing (450 °C/1 h) of the 8Al steel: YS rises from 540 to 990 MPa and UTS from 895 to 1180 MPa, while uniform elongation falls from 65% to 37%.

The precipitation state of the long annealed 8Al steel yields a remarkable increase in yield strength compared to the 2Al steel in solid solution (YS = 420 MPa for 2Al vs YS = 990 MPa for long annealed 8Al).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Crossbeam instrument (XB 1540, Carl Zeiss SMT AG, Germany) with an EBSD-based set-up for controlled diffraction conditions
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Long annealed 8Al steel tensile deformed to 0.15 true strain; longitudinal section with observation direction perpendicular to the tensile axis
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the dislocation patterning / planar dislocation substructures of the deformed long annealed 8Al steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Planar dislocation substructures consisting of dense dislocation arrays spaced between 100 and 300 nm; cuboidal κ-carbides sheared by dislocations within the arrays.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Phillips CM20 microscope; thin foils electropolished in 30% nitric acid in methanol at −30 °C and 10 V
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Long annealed 8Al sample; 20 nm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Image the distribution of κ-carbides and assess particle shearing in the long annealed 8Al steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Bright cuboidal κ-carbides (10 × 20 nm) arranged in rows separated by narrow matrix channels; sheared particles indicated by arrows; confirms uniform intragranular distribution.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Diffraction pattern of the long annealed 8Al precipitation state
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the crystal structure and orientation relationship of the κ-carbides
characterization_methods.key_findings: Confirms the κ-carbides maintain a cube/cube orientation relationship with the austenite matrix.

characterization_methods.technique: Tensile testing (to failure and interrupted to different strain levels)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, initial strain rate 5 × 10^-4 s^-1, cylindrical specimens 6 mm diameter × 40 mm gauge
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure mechanical properties and study microstructural evolution as a function of strain
characterization_methods.key_findings: Long annealed 8Al: YS 990 MPa, UTS 1180 MPa, UE 37%; nearly linear flow curve indicating a single hardening regime.

unmapped_findings: The 8Al steels exhibit less hardening capacity than the 2Al steels (early-stage hardening: 2Al ~2.6 GPa; 8Al ~2 GPa) and contain a single hardening regime that remains fairly constant during deformation; the short annealed 8Al steel exhibits greater hardening than the long annealed 8Al steel.
Despite the low strain hardening capacity of the long annealed 8Al steel (YS 990 MPa; UTS 1180 MPa), the alloy exhibits a considerably high ductility (UE 37%).

Similar precipitation states to that of the long annealed 8Al steel have been reported in annealed Fe–Mn–Al–C steels between 450 and 650 °C, with yield strength values up to 1400 MPa attained in ultrahigh carbon (1.8 wt.%) Fe–Mn–Al–C steels.
